items.problem: A CLI or an API a task builds is never tried, and nothing is tried in the task's own environment: only pages are tried, by a headless Chromium on the host with the network off, also for full-review work and on a PC where Docker is ready (where the task itself ran in the container, ADR 0101). The owner's decision (3) says work a person will use (a page, an app, a CLI, an API) is started in its own environment (the Docker sandbox on the owner's PC) and used as a person would.
items.evidence: packages/capabilities/src/browser/try-page.ts:124-140 (pages only, chromium.launch on the host); packages/runtime/src/loop/try-it.ts; docs/decisions/0104-proportional-verification-of-code-tasks.md:66-79 ('The try runs on the host for every level in this version ...; trying inside the Docker sandbox and trying a CLI or an API are later work'); docs/status/handoff/NEXT-SESSION.md:130-141 (owner decisions of 2026-11-01) point (3); merge.problems_left[1] 'verification: no CLI or API try it'.
items.expected: Per the owner's decision (3): a CLI a task builds is run with sample input from its brief or criteria and an API it builds is started and called, and pages are opened, inside the task's sandbox lease (the container when Docker is ready, always for a full review), with outputs and screenshots as the critic's evidence; 'Reviewed and tried' only when something was tried; what could not be tried says why in 'See what was checked'. Tested in a composed runtime test (a CLI task, an API task, a page task with the fake engine) and a real-daemon case; F2's Linux Docker run walks it for real.
items.reason: Not the owner's choice: decision (3) already says what and where (a CLI, an API, in the Docker sandbox on the owner's PC); ADR 0104 called it 'later work', which is the phase C fixer's scope, not an owner decision, and 'accept page-only for this round' would re-open decision (3). No phaseE.json area owns the review path (try-it.ts, capabilities/browser, the sandbox lease), so it goes to a sixth phase E area, 'verification' (handoffs.json 'verification'), with C-3 and C-17.

items.evidence: packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:342-347 (work is 'removed' whenever a live run stopped and the task has no PR; the folder kind is not read) and :263-267; apps/ui/src/lib/task-actions.ts:106-115 (cancelWorkLine, the dialog); ADR 0105 point 2.
items.expected: A third wording for a linked folder ('Its run stops now; what it wrote stays in your folder.'), in the command, the Cancel dialog and the fake daemon; tested with a linked-folder project.
items.reason: Untrue sentence (design §5 rule 9); words in commands/task.ts and task-actions.ts.

items.problem: Chat: 'Skip the <title> task' becomes Pause; 'Skip the task "<title>"' fails with 'no task matches "task "...""'; when the task finished before Yes the reply is the raw 'Not done: task: illegal transition done -> cancelled.'; the read-back 'Cancel "X"? It is dropped.' does not say a running task's run stops and its work is removed.
items.evidence: packages/commands/src/intent.ts:806-813 (skip -> task.pause) and :123-131 (taskName strips a trailing 'task' but not a leading 'task "..."'); packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:680-688 (raw 'illegal transition' text) and :230 (read-back); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1122 ('Not done: ...').
items.expected: 'skip the task "X"' finds X; the read-back says what Yes will do for a running task ('Cancel "X"? Its run stops now and what it changed is removed.'); a move the task can no longer make is said in words ('"X" is already done; nothing changed.'). Whether 'skip' means pause or cancel follows design §3.9 (say which in the commit). Tested at the chat boundary.
items.reason: Chat area work; answers owns intent.ts and the chat's command replies.

items.problem: github-result design choices: no Merge action in the app (merging stays level 3 Trusted, ADR 0062), no Inbox card or Update per waiting PR (the Overview is the one place), no PR/branch on the Changes page (it lists the person's own changes), no desktop shell change needed.

items.expected: As designed.
items.reason: Not-done items with design reasons; no person meets a problem.

items.problem: Repository projects: every task branches from origin/<default>, so a task that depends on a done task whose PR is not merged yet does not see that work (five sibling branches off main on the bench); with the real model the coder recreates files and a checker checks nothing.
items.evidence: packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:213-215 (createBranch from origin/<base>) and :238, :253 (rebase and changed files against origin/<base>); the critic's diff is origin/HEAD...HEAD (packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts).

items.reason: Owner's choice: stacked PRs (a dependent task's branch and PR base on its dependency's branch), or merge the dependencies' unmerged branches into the task's branch (the critic's diff then needs the same base), or hold a dependent task until its dependency's PR is merged.
items.owner_question: In a repository project, a task whose dependency's pull request is not merged yet: base its branch and PR on the dependency's branch (stacked PRs), merge the dependencies' unmerged branches into its branch, or hold it until the dependency's PR is merged?

items.problem: A run's reason is still cut at a dot inside a file name in one place: the 'could not do' line ('I could not complete this task. The file index.html cannot be created ...' becomes 'html cannot be created from it').

The file index.html cannot be created from it.') -> 'html cannot be created from it'. The failed-task line itself is fixed: quotedWords (packages/critic/src/followup.ts:100-104) keeps 'index.html' whole.
items.expected: couldNotWords uses the same sentence rule as quotedWords (a dot before a non-space does not end a sentence); a unit test with 'index.html' and 'data/members.csv'.
items.reason: The reported failed-task line was fixed by verification's quotedWords change; the sibling in couldNotWords is still true. Words in the session log.

items.problem: There is no web search on an API key: the researcher reads only pages the brief or the plan names.
items.evidence: packages/capabilities has no search capability; ADR 0107 records it; packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:720-728 (NO_WEB_SEARCH_LINE); the owner's decision: 'web access on the API-key path through Forerunner's own fetch/search capability, within the network rules' (docs/status/handoff/NEXT-SESSION.md:142-143).
items.expected: The owner's answer recorded in ADR 0107; if a search service is chosen, a 'web_search' capability behind the same network rules as web_fetch.
items.reason: Partly answered: the owner asked for Forerunner's own search within the network rules, so Anthropic's server-side search (outside the runtime's hooks) is not an option to offer. What remains is the owner's: a search service needs its own account, key and cost.
items.owner_question: Web search on an API key (you asked for Forerunner's own, within its network rules) needs a search service with its own key and cost: add one now (you pick the service and create its key), or keep page reading only (pages the brief or plan names) for this round?

items.problem: On a Claude subscription, research reads no page: the hooks deny every WebFetch because the researcher's and science-evaluator's allowed_domains are empty (only WebSearch works). Until the person chooses an order, tasks use the subscription first, so an install with both a subscription and an API key sends research to this path.
items.evidence: packages/runtime/src/agent/cc-tools.ts:77-82 (WebFetch domainFields ['url']); evals/registry/specialists/researcher/specialist.md:15 and science-evaluator/specialist.md:15 (allowed_domains: []); packages/runtime/test/security-sdk.test.ts asserts the denial; packages/runtime/src/daemon/billing-order-types.ts:48-52 and docs/user-guide.md:486-487 ('Until you choose an order, tasks use the subscription first').
items.expected: The owner's choice; the user guide then says what is true (C-71).
items.reason: The owner's research decision names the API-key path only, and opening the SDK path's WebFetch is a security change, so it is the owner's. The earlier reason ('API key billing first makes the API-key path the one used') does not hold by default: with both credentials saved and no order chosen, tasks go to the subscription first.
items.owner_question: On a Claude subscription the researcher reads no web page (search only), and tasks use the subscription first until you choose an order: let the subscription's WebFetch read public pages under the same rules as on the API key, send research tasks to the API key whenever one is saved, or keep the subscription search-only and say so?
